stories.head: Impulse Space raises $500 million for orbital taxis
stories.body: Impulse Space has secured $500 million, capitalizing on the burgeoning demand for orbital transportation services. This funding reflects a broader trend where investors are betting on the commercial viability of space taxis, an area previously thought to be a niche market. The influx of cash underscores the growing realization that transporting goods and personnel to orbit is not just a novelty, but a necessity.
stories.soWhat: If you thought space was just for satellites, think again—orbital taxis are now a serious business.

stories.head: Voyager to acquire Astrobotic for lunar ambitions
stories.body: Voyager has announced its acquisition of lunar lander developer Astrobotic, a move that positions the company to capitalize on the upcoming lunar missions. Astrobotic's experience in landing payloads on the Moon aligns well with Voyager's strategic goals, especially as NASA ramps up its Artemis program. The deal's financial details remain under wraps, but it’s clear that lunar real estate is heating up.
stories.soWhat: In a game where landing on the Moon is the new gold rush, partnering with a proven player is a smart, if not essential, move.

stories.head: FY27 budget adds $1.4B for space resilience
stories.body: The latest markup for the FY27 budget reveals a $1.4 billion increase in funding dedicated to space resilience. This marks a significant shift as defense priorities now explicitly recognize the importance of securing space assets. The implications for contractors and startups in the space sector are profound, as they may soon find themselves at the forefront of national security strategies.
stories.soWhat: When the government starts throwing money at space resilience, it’s time to dust off those proposals and get in line.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's Series C implications
watchlist.body: With a $190 million Series C, True Anomaly's valuation of $1.6 billion indicates strong investor confidence in co-orbital security solutions.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser progress
watchlist.body: Clearing the critical design review is a positive step, but the real test will be whether it can actually make it to orbit.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris collaboration insights
watchlist.body: Their joint bid on the tactical SDA constellation could reshape how the military approaches space situational awareness.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension impact
watchlist.body: With a $480 million contract extension, Palantir's grip on government contracts shows no signs of weakening, reinforcing its position in the defense sector.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
